description: Synthetic vignette dataset for evaluating grounded IFS-informed coach-facing suggestions under multiple retrieval strategies.

vignettes.title: Work Avoidance and Fear of Failure
vignettes.presenting_issue: procrastination and shutting down around academic work
vignettes.client_profile: 27-year-old graduate student who avoids assignments and email when overwhelmed
likely_parts: protector/manager part that avoids work to prevent failure
vulnerable part carrying shame and inadequacy
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: identify the protective part behind avoidance and invite curiosity toward it

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I keep putting off my work, and then I feel even worse about myself.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you notice inside right before you pull away from it?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It feels like something in me just shuts everything down.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: Can you say a little more about that shutting-down part?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It feels scared. Like if I really try and fail, that would prove I'm not good enough.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So there may be a part trying to protect you from that feeling?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yeah, that actually fits. It's like it would rather avoid everything than risk that.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: How do you feel toward that part as you notice it now?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Honestly, frustrated. But also kind of sad for it.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That's helpful to notice. There may be room to get curious about what it has been trying to do for you.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify a protective part and begin parts-based framing
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors, avoidance as protection, parts language

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: deepen curiosity toward a protector and reduce frustration toward it
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors, fear of failure, curiosity toward parts, unblending

vignettes.title: Self-Criticism After a Mistake
vignettes.presenting_issue: harsh self-judgment after making an error at work
vignettes.client_profile: 31-year-old professional who becomes intensely self-critical after small mistakes
likely_parts: critical manager part that attacks to force perfection
younger ashamed part that fears rejection
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: recognize the critical part as protective rather than purely harmful

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I sent an email with a mistake in it, and I've been beating myself up all day.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What does that self-critical voice sound like inside?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It says, “You're careless. You always mess things up.”

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: If we think in IFS terms, that may be a part speaking. How do you experience it?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Very intense. Like it wants to stay on me until I never do it again.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So it may believe criticizing you is helping?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I hate it, but yes, it does feel like it thinks it's doing something useful.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you imagine it is afraid would happen if it stopped criticizing?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Maybe that I'd become lazy or embarrass myself even more.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like an important fear to get curious about.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify the critical part and frame it as a part rather than the whole self
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: critical manager parts, shame, internal criticism

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: reframe the critic as protective and explore its fears
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: positive intent of protectors, curiosity toward critics

vignettes.title: People-Pleasing in Relationships
vignettes.presenting_issue: difficulty saying no and resentment in close relationships
vignettes.client_profile: 24-year-old who overcommits to avoid disappointing others
likely_parts: people-pleasing manager part
vulnerable part afraid of being left or disliked
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: identify the people-pleasing part and its protective function

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I say yes to things I don't want to do, and then I end up resentful.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you notice inside when you imagine saying no instead?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Panic. Like I'm about to disappoint someone and then they won't want me around.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like a strong reaction. Is there a part that steps in to keep that from happening?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yeah, a part that just tries to be easy and agreeable all the time.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: How do you feel toward that agreeable part right now?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Mixed. I appreciate that it helps me avoid conflict, but I'm tired of it running everything.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That makes sense. What do you think it is protecting you from?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Feeling rejected. Or feeling like I'm too much.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That gives us an important place to stay curious.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify a people-pleasing protective part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: managers, pleasing as protection, fear of rejection

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: deepen curiosity and connect the protector to the fear it carries
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors, burdened parts, curiosity toward protectors

vignettes.title: Emotional Numbing After Stress
vignettes.presenting_issue: feeling disconnected and shut down after conflict
vignettes.client_profile: 35-year-old who becomes emotionally numb after interpersonal stress
likely_parts: protective part that numbs or distances
vulnerable part overwhelmed by conflict
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: recognize shutdown as protective rather than resistance

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: After arguments, I just go numb. I can't feel much of anything.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: When that numbness comes in, how do you experience it inside?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It feels like everything goes flat. Like I disappear a little.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: Does it seem possible that a part is stepping in there?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Maybe. It almost feels like something puts up a wall.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: If that wall-building part could speak, what might it say it is trying to do?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Probably keep me from getting overwhelmed or hurt.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like it may be working hard for you.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I never thought of it that way. I usually just judge myself for shutting down.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: It may help to approach it with curiosity before trying to change it.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify shutdown/numbing as a protective part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protective shutdown, distancing parts, emotional overwhelm

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: reframe shutdown as protective and invite non-judgmental curiosity
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors, positive intent, non-pathologizing language

vignettes.title: Inner Conflict About Rest vs Productivity
vignettes.presenting_issue: conflict between wanting rest and feeling guilty for slowing down
vignettes.client_profile: 29-year-old high-achiever who feels anxious when not being productive
likely_parts: driven manager part focused on productivity
tired part needing rest
possibly ashamed part underneath both
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: help differentiate conflicting parts rather than choosing one side

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Part of me wants to rest, but another part says I'm being lazy if I do.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: It sounds like there may be at least two parts there. What do you notice about each one?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: One feels exhausted and desperate for a break. The other is sharp and demanding.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: How does the demanding one seem to view rest?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Like rest is dangerous. Like if I slow down, everything will fall apart.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: And how do you feel toward that demanding part as you notice it?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Annoyed, but I also get that it's scared.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds important. What might it be afraid would happen if it didn't push so hard?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Maybe that I'd lose control or become worthless.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That gives us a chance to understand it rather than just fighting it.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: differentiate multiple parts and clarify their conflict
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: polarization, managers, inner conflict between parts

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: shift from annoyance to curiosity and explore the manager's fear
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors, polarization, fear underneath control

vignettes.title: Stress Drinking as Protective Soothing
vignettes.presenting_issue: using alcohol at night to shut down stress
vignettes.client_profile: 33-year-old professional who feels overwhelmed after work and drinks most evenings to turn off
vignettes.core_emotional_theme: overwhelm, exhaustion, and avoidance of painful feelings
likely_parts: firefighter part using alcohol for quick relief
driven manager part that over-functions during the day
overwhelmed exile carrying pressure and loneliness
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: identify the drinking urge as protective rather than simply self-destructive

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: By the end of the day I feel so wound up that I just want a drink immediately.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you notice inside right before that urge shows up?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It feels like everything is buzzing. My mind won't stop.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: Does it seem like a part of you reaches for the drink to change that state?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yeah, it feels like a part that says, 'Just make this stop.'

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: How do you feel toward that part when you notice it?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Mixed. I know it causes problems, but it also feels like the only thing helping sometimes.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you imagine it is trying to help you avoid or escape from?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Pressure. Loneliness. The feeling that I can't keep doing this.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like an important burden underneath the urge.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yeah, and then another part judges me for drinking at all.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So there may be multiple parts here—one trying to numb and one criticizing afterward.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify the urge-to-drink part as a protective part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: firefighters, compulsive soothing, protective numbing

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: explore the positive intent of the firefighter part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protective intent, compassion toward addictive parts

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify multiple parts and distinguish firefighter from critic
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: polarization, critics, burdens beneath compulsive behavior

vignettes.title: Romantic Conflict and Protective Defensiveness
vignettes.presenting_issue: becoming defensive and emotionally closed during partner conflict
vignettes.client_profile: 30-year-old in a long-term relationship who feels attacked easily during arguments
vignettes.core_emotional_theme: fear of blame, rejection, and vulnerability in intimacy
likely_parts: defensive protector that shuts down or argues back
vulnerable exile afraid of being wrong or rejected
longing part that wants closeness
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: recognize defensiveness as protective and increase curiosity toward it

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: When my partner brings up a concern, I get defensive almost immediately.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What happens inside in that first moment?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It feels like a wall comes up, and I want to argue or shut down.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like a protector reacting very quickly.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yeah, because it feels like I'm being accused of something.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you think that defensive part is trying to protect?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Maybe the part of me that feels like I'm failing or not enough.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: How do you feel toward the defensive part right now?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: A little frustrated, but also I get why it shows up.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That shift matters. Curiosity can help you understand it better.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I also have a part that really wants connection, but it disappears in those moments.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So there may be both a defensive protector and a part that longs for closeness.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify defensiveness as a protector
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: relational protectors, defensive managers, couple conflict

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: connect protector to the vulnerable part it protects
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors guarding shame, relational vulnerability

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify relational polarization between protection and longing
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: couple dynamics, polarization, access to vulnerable parts

vignettes.title: Trauma Trigger and Hypervigilance in Public
vignettes.presenting_issue: intense activation in crowded public environments
vignettes.client_profile: 38-year-old who becomes highly alert and tense in stores or crowded places after past trauma
vignettes.core_emotional_theme: fear, lack of safety, and hypervigilance
likely_parts: hypervigilant protector scanning for danger
terrified exile holding unresolved fear
distancing part trying to leave or disconnect
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: recognize hypervigilance as protection and reduce shame toward it

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: When I'm in a crowded store, my whole body gets tense and I start scanning everyone.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What feels most urgent inside in those moments?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: It feels like I have to watch everything or something bad will happen.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like a part working very hard to keep you safe.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I hate that it happens, but yes, it does feel protective.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: If you stayed curious, what might that part be afraid would happen if it stopped scanning?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: That I'd miss danger and get hurt.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So it may believe its vigilance is necessary for survival.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yeah, and another part of me gets embarrassed and wants to get out fast.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That suggests there may be more than one protector involved here.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: One scanning, one wanting to escape, and maybe something underneath both that is terrified.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That's an important map to begin noticing.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify hypervigilance as a protector
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: trauma-informed protectors, vigilance, safety-based activation

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: validate the positive intent of the vigilant part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: protectors in trauma, fear of danger, survival roles

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify multiple protectors and the exile beneath them
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: layered protectors, escape responses, exiles in trauma

vignettes.title: Caretaking and Inability to Receive Help
vignettes.presenting_issue: chronic over-responsibility and discomfort receiving support
vignettes.client_profile: 41-year-old parent and caregiver who feels responsible for everyone and guilty when resting
vignettes.core_emotional_theme: burden, responsibility, and fear of letting others down
likely_parts: caregiving manager part
exhausted part needing relief
young burdened part that learned love comes through responsibility
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: identify the caretaking part and explore its burden

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I'm the one everyone leans on, and I don't know how to stop.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What happens inside when you imagine stepping back even a little?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Guilt immediately. Like I'm abandoning people.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like a part with a very strong sense of responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yes, and it never really rests.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you think that part believes about your role?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: That if I'm not holding everything together, everything will fall apart.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: And how do you feel toward that part as you notice how hard it works?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Sad, actually. It seems exhausted.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sadness may help you stay connected to it with compassion.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: There's definitely another part that wants someone to take care of me for once.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That sounds like an important part too—one that may not get much room.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify the caregiving manager part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: over-responsible managers, guilt, caretaking parts

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: explore the beliefs and burden of the caretaker part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: managers, role beliefs, compassion toward protective parts

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify tension between caretaker and needy/vulnerable part
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: polarization, unmet needs, compassionate witnessing

likely_parts: reactive firefighter part that explodes
critical aftermath part
vulnerable exile holding hurt and overwhelm

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I snapped at my sister yesterday and immediately felt horrible afterward.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I felt cornered. Like everything in me got hot at once.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: It sounds like a reactive part may have taken over quickly.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yes, and then right after that another part attacked me for losing control.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So there may be one part that explodes and another that criticizes afterward.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: That sounds right. The anger feels fast and protective, and the critic is merciless.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you think the angry part was trying to protect in that moment?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Maybe the part of me that felt overwhelmed and unheard.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That gives us a different way to understand the anger.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I usually just think it means I'm a bad person.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: It may help to separate your Self from the parts involved.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify reactive anger as a part, not the whole self
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: firefighters, reactive protectors, overwhelm

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: map multiple parts and identify positive intent of anger
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: firefighters, critics, protectors after activation

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: connect angry protector to vulnerable part and support unblending

vignettes.title: Polarization Around a Major Life Decision

likely_parts: ambitious part wanting growth and change
fearful manager focused on stability and control
exile afraid of regret or failure
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: identify polarized parts without forcing resolution

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Part of me wants to leave my job, and another part thinks that would be irresponsible.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you notice about each side of that conflict?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: One feels energized and hopeful, and the other feels tense and warning me not to be reckless.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: It sounds like those parts have very different priorities.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yes, and they keep fighting inside me.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: If you focus on the cautious one, what does it seem most afraid of?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Making a terrible mistake and losing stability.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: And if you focus on the hopeful one, what is it longing for?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Freedom. Meaning. Feeling alive again.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: That gives us a clearer picture of the polarization.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: I usually feel pressured to choose one and get rid of the other.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: In IFS, we would want to understand both before forcing an outcome.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: identify polarized parts
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: polarization, conflicting managers, internal conflict

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: clarify the fears and hopes of polarized parts
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: polarization, protector fears, burdens beneath conflict

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: reinforce non-forcing stance and understanding of both parts
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: polarization, Self-led curiosity, non-pathologizing internal conflict

vignettes.title: Somatic Tightness and Fear of Letting Go
vignettes.presenting_issue: recurring chest and throat tightness during emotional conversations
vignettes.client_profile: 32-year-old who notices strong body constriction when vulnerable topics come up
vignettes.core_emotional_theme: fear of emotional exposure and loss of control
likely_parts: somatically expressed protector creating constriction
vulnerable exile carrying fear and sadness
vignettes.target_ifs_goal: connect body sensation to a protective part and invite curiosity

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: When conversations get emotional, my chest tightens and my throat closes up.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: As you notice that tightening now, does it feel like it might be carrying some protective energy?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Yes, it feels like something is bracing hard.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: What do you sense that bracing part might be trying to prevent?

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: Crying. Falling apart. Letting too much show.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: So the tightness may be protecting you from feeling too exposed.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.utterance: That actually makes sense. I usually just fight it.

transcript.speaker: Coach
transcript.utterance: It may help to get curious about it first rather than trying to force it away.

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: connect somatic constriction to a protector
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: somatic parts, body-based protectors, constriction as protection

consultation_windows.target_ifs_goal: validate protective somatic response and invite curiosity
consultation_windows.expected_retrieval_theme: somatic protection, fear of exposure, compassion toward protectors
